# Technical Presentations

## Purpose

Use this skill for repository-local HTML presentations.

It covers:

- Creating a deck
- Editing an existing deck
- Running the development server
- Building static presentation output
- Validating metadata, links, accessibility, layouts, interactions, and print
- Publishing individual deck paths through GitHub Pages
- Troubleshooting common authoring and build failures

Do not use this workflow to edit a PowerPoint file. Use the PPTX workflow when the requested input or output is `.pptx`, `.potx`, SharePoint PowerPoint, or OneDrive PowerPoint.

## Required context

Before editing:

1. Read `/design.md`.
2. Read `/README.md`.
3. Read the target deck's `/decks/<id>/deck.json`.
4. Read the target deck's `/decks/<id>/sources.md`.
5. Read `/brands/<brand>/README.md` and the selected theme.
6. Check `/CONTRIBUTING.md` for the completion checklist.

Official brand guidance overrides repository guidance. Never copy protected presentation-template imagery or long passages from brand guides.

## Repository model

```text
decks/<id>/           Deck-specific content and visuals
src/runtime/          Shared navigation and progressive-build behavior
src/styles/           Shared presentation styles and print rules
brands/               Brand tokens and themes
templates/            New-deck starter files
scripts/              Scaffolding and validation tools
tests/                Playwright presentation checks
.github/              CI, Pages deployment, and contribution controls
```

Never edit:

- `dist/` — generated by Vite
- `node_modules/` — generated by npm
- External brand PDFs or internal presentation templates

## Command reference

Install dependencies locally:

```bash
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
```

Use deterministic dependency installation in CI or a clean environment:

```bash
npm ci
```

Start the authoring server:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open a deck directly:

```text
http://localhost:5173/decks/<id>/
```

Validate manifests and local links:

```bash
npm run validate
```

Build all decks:

```bash
npm run build
```

Preview the production build:

```bash
npm run preview
```

Run browser and accessibility tests:

```bash
npm test
```

Run the complete repository gate:

```bash
npm run check
```

## Create a new deck

Collect these requirements first:

- Deck ID in lowercase kebab-case
- Title
- Audience
- Delivery duration
- Measurable learning objectives
- Brand profile
- Theme
- Narrative scenario
- Authoritative sources
- Delivery mode: live, self-guided, workshop, or reference

Create a GitHub Default deck:

```bash
npm run new:deck -- \
  --id platform-overview \
  --title "Platform Overview" \
  --brand github \
  --theme default-dark
```

Create a GitHub Copilot deck:

```bash
npm run new:deck -- \
  --id ghcp-overview \
  --title "GitHub Copilot" \
  --brand github \
  --theme copilot-dark
```

Create a GitHub Advanced Security deck:

```bash
npm run new:deck -- \
  --id ghas-overview \
  --title "GitHub Advanced Security" \
  --brand github \
  --theme security-dark
```

Create a brand-neutral deck:

```bash
npm run new:deck -- \
  --id technical-briefing \
  --title "Technical Briefing" \
  --brand neutral
```

The scaffolder creates:

```text
decks/<id>/
├── index.html
├── deck.js
├── deck.css
├── deck.json
└── sources.md
```

After scaffolding:

1. Complete `deck.json`.
2. Replace starter learning objectives.
3. Add all authoritative sources to `sources.md`.
4. Establish one scenario or narrative spine.
5. Replace placeholder text and visuals.
6. Run `npm run validate` before substantial design work.

Only one deck may set `"default": true`. The root `index.html` must redirect to that deck.

## Select a GitHub theme

Supported GitHub themes:

- `default-dark`
- `default-light`
- `copilot-dark`
- `copilot-light`
- `security-dark`
- `security-light`

Theme selection rules:

- Use Default for general GitHub platform or company content.
- Use Copilot for GitHub Copilot and AI-led content.
- Use Security for GitHub Advanced Security, code security, supply-chain security, and trust content.
- GitHub Green remains the connective brand thread.
- Copilot purple and Security blue support the GitHub brand; they do not replace it.

The values in `deck.json`, the HTML `data-brand`, and the HTML `data-theme` must match.

## Edit an existing deck

Deck-specific changes belong in:

- `index.html` for slide structure and accessible content
- `deck.css` for deck-specific visual design
- `deck.js` for deck-specific interactions and data
- `deck.json` for metadata
- `sources.md` for provenance

Put reusable behavior in:

- `src/runtime/deck.js`
- `src/styles/`

Do not copy shared navigation or progressive-build code into a deck.

Use semantic variables such as:

```css
var(--color-page)
var(--color-canvas)
var(--color-panel)
var(--color-text)
var(--color-text-muted)
var(--color-accent)
var(--color-accent-secondary)
var(--color-link)
```

Avoid hard-coded organization colors when a brand token exists.

## Progressive builds

Use `data-build-step` for presenter-controlled disclosure:

```html
<article class="card">Visible immediately</article>
<article class="card" data-build-step="1">First reveal</article>
<article class="card" data-build-step="2">Second reveal</article>
```

Runtime behavior:

- Space, Right Arrow, or Page Down reveals the next build before changing slides.
- Left Arrow or Page Up reverses the current slide's latest build before moving backward.
- Home resets all builds and returns to the first slide.
- Print mode reveals all build content.
- Reduced-motion mode removes unnecessary animation.

Do not use timed automatic reveals for live technical presentations.

## Sources and downloadable artifacts

Every deck must maintain `sources.md`.

Record:

- Product documentation
- Brand guidance
- Research and metrics
- Diagram inspiration
- External imagery
- Code samples
- Access date when content may change

Deck-specific downloads belong under:

```text
decks/<id>/examples/
decks/<id>/assets/
```

The Vite build copies deck support files into the corresponding `dist/decks/<id>/` path.

## Deck-specific validators

A deck may declare validators in `deck.json`:

```json
{
  "validators": [
    {
      "name": "Example compiler",
      "command": "tool validate examples/example.md"
    }
  ]
}
```

Run every declared validator before completion.

For the GH-AW deck:

```bash
cd decks/gh-aw
gh aw compile examples/repo-care.md \
  --dir examples \
  --no-emit \
  --validate \
  --strict \
  --schedule-seed demo/gh-agentic-workflows \
  --no-check-update
```

## Quality gate

Before declaring a deck complete:

1. Run `npm run validate`.
2. Run `npm run build`.
3. Run `npm test`.
4. Run deck-specific validators.
5. Inspect affected slides visually.
6. Confirm no test screenshots, Playwright metadata, or temporary downloads remain.

Browser tests cover:

- 1366x768
- 1200x796
- 1920x1080
- Console errors
- Primary layout clipping
- Code-window overflow
- Keyboard build behavior
- Serious accessibility violations
- Print behavior
- Existing GH-AW interactions

Manual review must still check:

- Narrative clarity
- Visual hierarchy
- Projector readability
- Brand restraint
- Diagram meaning
- Source-note collisions
- Excessive density
- Misleading color semantics

## Build and publish

Build output is written to:

```text
dist/
```

Individual decks retain direct paths:

```text
dist/decks/gh-aw/
dist/decks/ghas-overview/
dist/decks/ghcp-overview/
```

The GitHub Pages workflow:

1. Installs dependencies
2. Builds all decks
3. Runs browser tests
4. Uploads `dist/`
5. Deploys individual deck URLs

Pushes to `main` trigger deployment when GitHub Pages is enabled for GitHub Actions.

## Troubleshooting

### `deck.json` validation fails

Check:

- Directory name matches `id`
- Exactly one deck is the default
- Brand and theme are supported
- `sources.md` exists
- HTML brand/theme attributes match metadata

Run:

```bash
npm run validate
```

### Theme is not configured

Confirm the file exists:

```text
brands/<brand>/themes/<theme>.css
```

Do not invent Microsoft theme tokens. Use the neutral profile until approved Microsoft guidance is available.

### A local download works in development but not in `dist`

Place the file inside the deck folder under `examples/` or `assets/`, then rebuild. The Vite deck-copy plugin publishes non-code deck support files.

### A slide clips at one viewport

- Reduce text density before reducing font size.
- Shorten labels.
- Reserve fixed title heights for card rows.
- Move secondary detail into progressive builds.
- Keep sources clear of the content region.

### Playwright reports a print failure

Ensure print CSS sets hidden builds to visible and disables transitions:

```css
@media print {
  [data-build-step] {
    opacity: 1 !important;
    visibility: visible !important;
    transform: none !important;
    transition: none !important;
  }
}
```

### GitHub Pages assets fail under nested paths

- Use relative deck links.
- Import shared modules through Vite.
- Do not hard-code a repository name into asset URLs.
- Verify the built HTML references `../../assets/` from nested deck paths.

## Completion response

When reporting completed work:

- Name the deck or platform area changed.
- Summarize the meaningful content, design, or interaction improvement.
- Mention a command only when the user needs it to run or open the result.
